overview: This Senate resolution designates October 2026 as "National Country Music Month." It celebrates country music as a uniquely American genre, mentions landmarks such as Bristol on the Tennessee-Virginia line, the Grand Ole Opry and the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, and notes the industry's contribution to the economy. It also notes the death of Dolly Parton on August 25, 2026. The resolution honors the genre and its stars and encourages Americans to mark the month with ceremonies and activities. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 23, 2026.
for: Supporters say country music is an important part of American culture and history, and the month recognizes its artists and the communities it comes from.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
